newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia stocks finish sleepy session firmer.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stocks finish sleepy session firmer.

text.p: SPI Futures cl 2386 +1 US 30yr 6.61 +0.02
10yrbond futs 92.460 -0.070 Gold NY 368.75 Lon fix 369.20
*Stocks ended a quiet session slightly firmer with the bank sector lending support. Volume 285.6 million, value A$569.8 million, 1,050 stocks traded, 289 steady, 438 up, 323 down.
Australian shares edged to a slightly higher close on Monday with light buying interest in the bank sector supporting the market as it wound down for the festive season.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed 6.7 points higher at 2,380.5, not far from its intra-day high of 2,384.7.
December share price index futures finished one point firmer at 2,386, a 5.5 point premium to the underlying index a week away from the contract's expiry.
Turnover was about a third of the market's record one session volume of A$1.7 billion, which was set on Friday.
"It was the sort of trade you expect for this time of year - fairly lumpy. I certainly wouldn't want to read to much into it," a Sydney-based dealer said.

The dealer said the two factors supporting the market on the day were some selective bargain hunting and interest in the bank sector following the Advance Bank shareholder's approval of a scheme to merge with fellow regional St George Bank.
"The approval appears to clinch the deal for St George and although this was bad for its shares, it was good for Advance and National Australia Bank stock," the dealer said.
In other trading, Australian bonds drifted lower during a thin pre-Christmas session with sellers gaining the upper hand after Friday's easier trend in U.S. Treasuries.
The yield on 10-year T-bonds closed at 7.45 percent, 0.07 percentage points higher than Monday's close.
The Australian dollar inched up to its highest level for a fortnight Monday, although dealers said the gains owed more to an illiquid market than real demand.
At 5.10 p.m. (0610 GMT), the unit was quoted at US$0.7959/64, bouncing solidly from the US$0.7915 level late last week.

St George Bank stock slipped after it moved one step closer to gaining control of Advance after Advance shareholders approved a merger scheme, while Advance and National Australia stock benefited from the vote, dealers said. *Highlands A$0.77 (+.02) 0.751/0.77 Vol: 966,876 Highlands rejected Placer Dome Inc's 75 cents per share citing an independent report showing its shares to be worth about 40 pct more than the offer. Placer Dome later said it would cancel its 33 percent stake in Highlands for Highlands' 25 percent stake in the Porgera gold project in Papua New Guinea.
